name: AppsSection links not working
description:
## Conversation Summary

1. **Reported issue:** App links (New, Task Manager, Planning, Messenger, Meet, File Explorer, Wiki) didn't respond to clicks.
2. **First fix:** Repointed `AppsSection.vue` from the broken `this.$ui.setActiveTab()` path to the working `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.openApp()` API.
3. **Real root cause:** `openApp()` decided between dockview panels and route navigation using a screen-width check (`$storex.ui.isMobile`), so wide screens on non-desktop routes tried to create panels with no dockview mounted.
4. **Correct rule (as you specified):** Mode is defined by the **route** — `.../desktop` = Desktop mode (additive panels), any other route = Single mode (one app, via route path).
5. **Fix applied:** Added an `isDesktopMode()` helper in `src/router/navigate.js` (route name == `codx-junior-split`), made `openApp()` branch on it, and had the `$navigation.isDesktopMode` getter delegate to it as the single source of truth.

Let me inspect the sidebar components that actually trigger navigation. ``` Read 3 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue, src/components/layout/MobileBottomBar.vue, src/components/layout/ViewModeToggle.vue ``` ## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking **Core Requirements** The "APPS" links in `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` (New, Task Manager, Planning, Messenger, Meet, File Explorer, Wiki) do nothing when clicked. **Root Cause (traced through the codebase)** Every app-opening path eventually needs the navigation layer, whose **correct** location — proven by the components that *do* work — is `this.$storex.$router.$navigation`: - `App.vue` → `$storex.$router.$navigation.getChatId()` - `DesktopSidebar.vue` → `$storex.$router.$navigation.getWorkspaceId()` / `.isDesktopMode` - `MobileBottomBar.vue` → `$storex.$router.$navigation.apps.openKanban()` / `.openFileExplorer()` / `.openHome()` - `ViewModeToggle.vue` → `$storex.$router.$navigation.isDesktopMode` / `.apps.openHome()` / `.apps.openDesktop()` `AppsSection.vue`, however, opens its links via `this.$ui.setActiveTab(appKey)`. In the UI store that mutation delegates to the `openApp` action, which currently looks up the wrong object (`$storex.$navigation`, which is undefined) and bails out with a warning — so nothing opens. The same component also reads `this.$ui.isDesktopMode`, which is not part of the navigation API used everywhere else. **Strategic Approach** Repoint `AppsSection.vue`'s opener to the same navigation object the other working components use (`this.$storex.$router.$navigation`), and align the desktop-mode check with `$navigation.isDesktopMode`. This fixes the links regardless of the store's internal lookup. **Dependencies & Risks** - Root-cause note: `src/store/ui.js` → `openApp` reads `$storex.$navigation` instead of `$storex.$router.$navigation`; fixing that one line would repair *all* store-routed links app-wide (recommended follow-up, but out of scope for this single-file fix). - `$navigation.openApp(appKey, data)` is the generic entry point already used by the store, so no per-app method names need to be guessed. **Target Files** - Modify `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` ## 2. Minimum Changes Approach Single file, `methods` section only: 1. `openApp(appKey)` → call `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.openApp(appKey, {})`. 2. `handleNavigateToNewChat()` → read `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.isDesktopMode` (consistent with `ViewModeToggle`/`DesktopSidebar`). Everything else (template, props, emits, structure) stays untouched. ## 3. File changes ```vue src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue ``` ## 4. File Change Summary Table | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` | Modify | `methods.openApp` | Replaced `this.$ui.setActiveTab(appKey)` (routes through the broken store lookup) with `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.openApp(appKey, {})`, the same navigation API used by `MobileBottomBar`/`ViewModeToggle`. | | `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` | Modify | `methods.handleNavigateToNewChat` | Replaced `this.$ui.isDesktopMode` with `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.isDesktopMode` for a consistent, reachable desktop-mode check. | ### Recommended follow-up (root cause, separate file) `src/store/ui.js` → `openApp` action resolves navigation from `$storex.$navigation`, but the object actually lives at `$storex.$router.$navigation`. Correcting that one line (`const navigation = $storex.$router.$navigation`) would restore every store-routed link app-wide. I left it out to keep this change scoped to the reported file — let me know if you'd like me to apply it.

1. The user reported that the "APPS" links (New, Task Manager, Planning, Messenger, Meet, File Explorer, Wiki) were not working.
2. Investigation traced the apps menu to `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue`, which opened links via `this.$ui.setActiveTab(appKey)`.
3. That store action resolved navigation from the nonexistent `$storex.$navigation`, so it silently bailed out — the correct path is `$storex.$router.$navigation`, confirmed by working components like `MobileBottomBar` and `ViewModeToggle`.
4. The fix repointed `openApp()` to `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.openApp(appKey, {})` and corrected the desktop-mode check in `handleNavigateToNewChat()`.
5. A recommended follow-up was flagged: fixing the single wrong lookup in `src/store/ui.js` would repair all store-routed app links project-wide.

## Conversation Summary

1. **Reported issue:** App links (New, Task Manager, Planning, Messenger, Meet, File Explorer, Wiki) didn't respond to clicks.
2. **First fix:** Repointed `AppsSection.vue` from the broken `this.$ui.setActiveTab()` path to the working `this.$storex.$router.$navigation.openApp()` API.
3. **Real root cause:** `openApp()` decided between dockview panels and route navigation using a screen-width check (`$storex.ui.isMobile`), so wide screens on non-desktop routes tried to create panels with no dockview mounted.
4. **Correct rule (as you specified):** Mode is defined by the **route** — `.../desktop` = Desktop mode (additive panels), any other route = Single mode (one app, via route path).
5. **Fix applied:** Added an `isDesktopMode()` helper in `src/router/navigate.js` (route name == `codx-junior-split`), made `openApp()` branch on it, and had the `$navigation.isDesktopMode` getter delegate to it as the single source of truth.
